steps.body: You now have one method for any unit rate with fractions: divide the two quantities by flipping the second fraction and multiplying. Mixed practice locks the method in.

predict.prompt: A hiker covers 5/8 mile in 5/16 hour. Is the unit rate more or less than 1 mile per hour?

options.label: More — 5/8 mile in well under half an hour is quick

predict.reveal: 5/16 hour is under a third of an hour, and 5/8 mile is covered in it. Scaling up to a full hour multiplies both by more than three — so the rate lands well above 1 mile per hour.

widget.prompt: The hiker's pace, in sixteenths of an hour. Fill in the distance at a full hour, keeping the ratio.
widget.successFeedback: 2 miles per hour. Each row keeps the same rate — 5/16 → 5/8, 10/16 → 10/8, 1 → 2 — and the awkward-looking fractions never had to become decimals. 5/8 ÷ 5/16 = 2.
widget.lowFeedback: Too short. A whole hour is sixteen sixteenths — more than three times the 5/16 in the first row.
widget.highFeedback: Too far. Check against the rows above: the distance grows by the same factor the time does.

widget.prompt: A snail covers 1/6 mile in 1/3 hour. What is the unit rate in miles per hour?

commonEntries.feedback: That flips the wrong fraction. (1/6) ÷ (1/3) = 1/2, not 2.
That multiplies directly instead of dividing. (1/6) ÷ (1/3) = 1/2.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Unit rate is distance ÷ time: (1/6) ÷ (1/3) — flip the TIME fraction and multiply.

steps.body: Whichever quantity comes first in the sentence goes on top — "miles per hour" means miles ÷ hours, always in that order.

widget.prompt: A pitcher fills 3/10 cup in 3/20 minute. Fill in the amount at a full minute, keeping the ratio.
widget.successFeedback: 2 cups per minute. Twentieths kept the whole table exact — 3/20 → 3/10, 6/20 → 6/10, 1 → 2 — and 3/10 ÷ 3/20 = 2, the same answer the rows walk you to.
widget.lowFeedback: Too little. A full minute is twenty twentieths, and the first row covers only three of them.
widget.highFeedback: Too much — more than the rate allows. Compare against the 6/20 → 6/10 row.

steps.body: If you ever get confused about which fraction to flip, remember: you're always dividing the FIRST quantity by the SECOND — flip the second one, then multiply.

widget.prompt: A painter covers 1/8 mile in 1/4 hour. What is the unit rate in miles per hour?

options.feedback: That flips the wrong fraction. (1/8) ÷ (1/4) = 1/2, not 2.
That multiplies directly instead of dividing. (1/8) ÷ (1/4) = 1/2.

widget.prompt: A biker covers 2/5 mile in 1/5 hour. What is the unit rate in miles per hour?

commonErrors.feedback: That multiplies the first fraction's numerator by its own denominator: 2×5=10, instead of flipping the second fraction and multiplying: (2/5)×5=2.

widget.prompt: A rower covers 1/3 mile in 2/3 hour. What is the unit rate in miles per hour?

commonEntries.feedback: That flips the wrong fraction. (1/3) ÷ (2/3) = 1/2, not 2.
That multiplies directly instead of dividing. (1/3) ÷ (2/3) = 1/2.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Unit rate is distance ÷ time: (1/3) ÷ (2/3) — flip the time fraction and multiply.

widget.prompt: A climber covers 7/16 mile in 7/8 hour. What is the unit rate in miles per hour?

commonEntries.feedback: That flips the wrong fraction. (7/16) ÷ (7/8) = 1/2, not 2.
That multiplies directly instead of dividing. (7/16) ÷ (7/8) = 1/2.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Unit rate is distance ÷ time: (7/16) ÷ (7/8) — flip the time fraction and multiply.

steps.body: One method — flip and multiply — finds any unit rate with fractions.
takeaways: Unit rate = first quantity ÷ second quantity.
Flip the second fraction, then multiply.
The result can be a whole number or a fraction — both are valid unit rates.

concept.body: For any unit rate with fractions: divide the first quantity by the second, by flipping the second fraction and multiplying. (5/8) ÷ (5/16) = (5/8) × (16/5) = 2.

widget.prompt: A hiker covers 5/8 mile in 5/16 hour. What is the unit rate in miles per hour?

commonErrors.feedback: That multiplies just the two numerators and drops both denominators: 5×5=25. Flip the second fraction and multiply completely: (5/8)×(16/5)=2.
